summary: Discovery call with AtlasAI to evaluate migrating from OpenAI-hosted endpoints to Redwood Dedicated (or Private). Key concerns: latency parity with current vLLM/TGI stack, inference compatibility (OpenAI API parity), security (VPC/KMS/SOC2), and benchmark plan. Agreed next steps: share pricing, security docs, run a 1-week eval with sample prompts, and schedule infra deep dive.
topics: Compatibility with OpenAI API and eval parity
Performance: vLLM/TGI parity and latency targets
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start time (UTC): 16:00
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (AtlasAI Head of ML), Noah Kim (Infra Lead), Evelyn Park (CTO)

Summary: quick discovery to understand AtlasAI's migration requirements from OpenAI to either Redwood Hosted/Dedicated/Private, and to validate performance parity with their current vLLM/TGI infra.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena Ortiz: hey everyone thanks for carving out time, um i'm lena from redwood, and with me is marcus who's our se, do you want to intro quick?
[00:18] Marcus Chen: yeah hi all marcus chen, se on infra and perf, i'll be focusing on benchmarks and the pci/ks -- sorry, the k-m-s integrations cause those are usually the sticky points.
[00:30] Priya Singh: thanks lena, i'm priya, lead ml at atlas, we run a mixture of hosted openai for prod and self-hosted v l l m and t g i for lower cost high throughput internal stuff.
[00:44] Noah Kim: noah here infra, we're trying to move more prod traffic off openai to reduce unit costs and control throughput, and also avoid data residency issues.
[00:55] Evelyn Park: evelyn, cto, just listening, main things for me are parity on quality and predictable latency.
[01:05] Lena Ortiz: great, quick agenda: 1) current stack & pain points, 2) compatibility concerns (openai api, model behaviours), 3) perf targets (latency, throughput), 4) security and deployment options, 5) pilot next steps. sound good?
[01:18] Priya Singh: yes, let's go.
[01:30] Marcus Chen: priya, can you give us a sense of the traffic profile? tokens per request, burstiness, and what percent is chat vs embeddings etc.
[01:45] Priya Singh: sure. roughly 60% chat-style generation, avg context 1.2k tokens, but we do lots of short queries too; embeddings are about 25% of traffic, batched in jobs. peak qps can spike to ~220 rps during business hours.
[02:02] Noah Kim: our SLA target is p95 < 350ms for single-turn prompts; that's been hard with our self-host stack at high concurrency.
[02:18] Marcus Chen: cool, that's helpful. on the compatibility side, are you using the OpenAI REST shapes heavily, function-calling, streaming?
[02:30] Priya Singh: yes to all — function calling for structured outputs is pretty essential, streaming for low latency UX, and we have prompt engineering tuned to the OpenAI response format.
[02:44] Lena Ortiz: good to know. Redwood's hosted API is OpenAI-like, and our Dedicated can be configured to accept OpenAI-compatible payloads. there are edge cases on exact tokenization and sampling seeds; we'll surface those in the eval.
[03:05] Priya Singh: quick q — we've heard mixed things about parity when you run on cpu-optimized stacks like vllm or t g i. how close is redwood to the outputs we get from openai?
[03:18] Marcus Chen: short answer: we aim for eval parity. in practice, differences come from model variant, quantization, and runtime kernels. for many customers we run side-by-side comparisons (n-gram overlap, rouge, and custom prompt evals) and we tune quantization and temperature to match.
[03:40] Evelyn Park: do you let us pin a model version? we can't have drift mid-promo.
[03:48] Lena Ortiz: yes, customers can pin model versions and we support rollouts/canaries.
[03:55] Noah Kim: on infra/security — we need VPC peering + customer KMS. can dedicated do that?
[04:05] Marcus Chen: yes, Dedicated supports VPC peering and Private offers a customer-managed control plane. we integrate with KMS/HSM, and we can provide audit logs and SOC2 artifacts. i'll note that for the security doc.
[04:20] Priya Singh: latency — you mentioned kernels and quantization; we've been using vLLM optimized kernels on A100s for our internal infra. what's your typical p95 on similar workloads?
[04:35] Marcus Chen: it varies by model and sequence length. for a 1.2k token chat on a 80k context model (well, hypothetical), p95 on Dedicated with batching tuned is around 200–320ms for gen-only, but with function-calling and streaming it's a bit higher. we'll run their exact prompt set.
[04:58] Priya Singh: that's promising. do you support custom kernels or can we provide a TGI/vllm launch config?
[05:08] Marcus Chen: we don't run third-party kernel binaries directly, but our runtime supports kernels tuned for the hardware and can mimic many performance knobs from vllm/TGI. for really custom stacks, our Private on-prem offering is more flexible.
[05:25] Lena Ortiz: also note that we can route requests: high priority low-latency traffic to dedicated pool and lower priority to cheaper variants — helps manage cost.
[05:38] Noah Kim: cost — what's the rough delta vs OpenAI for generation & embeddings?
[05:45] Lena Ortiz: depends on commit and utilization; generally our Dedicated unit costs can be 30–60% lower than public consumption prices for high volume customers once you factor in reserved capacity. we'll send a detailed quote.
[05:58] Priya Singh: regulatory — we need data residency in eu for some customers. can private or dedicated pin region?
[06:07] Marcus Chen: yes, Dedicated can be region pinned and Private can be fully customer-hosted in EU. we also offer audit logs and retention controls.
[06:16] Priya Singh: ok great.
[06:25] Evelyn Park: what's the pilot look like? we'd want to run evals to compare model outputs (quality), latency, and cost over 1 week.
[06:35] Marcus Chen: standard pilot is 1–4 weeks: we spin up a dedicated pool, run your prompt set across the models you need, collect metrics (tokens, latency p50/p95, cost), and a quality matrix. we also do a side-by-side OpenAI run for parity.
[06:50] Priya Singh: perfect. i'm worried about tokenization differences — we rely on exact string matches in some pipelines.
[06:58] Marcus Chen: totally, tokenization and stop-sequence behavior can cause diffs. we'll include token-level diffs and show how prompt tweaks affect outputs.
[07:10] Noah Kim: integration work — we currently call the OpenAI REST endpoints. how much effort to switch?
[07:18] Lena Ortiz: for many teams it's minimal — we support an OpenAI-compatible shim for our Hosted and Dedicated APIs. Special features (edge-case function-calling behaviour) may need small adjustments.
[07:32] Priya Singh: are there any known gotchas with streaming and function-calling?
[07:38] Marcus Chen: occasionally streaming chunk boundaries differ; function-calling parameter order might be returned differently by model variants. we log examples and recommend small prompt changes.
[07:50] Priya Singh: ok. on security again, can we do customer-managed keys and rotate keys on our schedule?
[07:58] Marcus Chen: yes, KMS integration allows rotation and we can map to customer principals; we provide key export logs for audits.
[08:10] Evelyn Park: SLA — uptime and latency SLO?
[08:16] Lena Ortiz: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; specific numbers in the proposal. for Hosted we have tiered SLAs for enterprise.
[08:27] Priya Singh: what about vendor lock-in concerns if we build more on your APIs?
[08:33] Lena Ortiz: we design for portability: same OpenAI-shaped API, exportable model artefacts where applicable, and a consistent rollout layer so you can move between Hosted, Dedicated, Private.
[08:47] Noah Kim: any customers who've done a full migration from OpenAI to Dedicated?
[08:53] Marcus Chen: yes — several mid-market customers; one did a 6-week pilot and cut unit cost by 45% while meeting p95 latency targets after kernel tuning. we can share a redacted case study.
[09:07] Priya Singh: we'll want to see that, and see benchmark numbers for similar context lengths.
[09:13] Lena Ortiz: noted.
[09:20] Priya Singh: can we talk about model licensing — some of our models are finetuned transformer variants we can't publicize. does Dedicated support private model uploads?
[09:31] Marcus Chen: yes, Private and Dedicated support customer model hosting with access controls; for proprietary finetunes we can ensure they never leave your VPC in Private deployments.
[09:42] Evelyn Park: good.
[09:48] Lena Ortiz: any blockers on your side for starting a pilot?
[09:54] Priya Singh: mainly legal review of the pilot contract and security questionnaires; and we need to confirm cost numbers.
[10:01] Noah Kim: and we'll want to run the vLLM/TGI baseline we already have so results are apples-to-apples.
[10:09] Marcus Chen: absolutely — we'll provide benchmark scripts and a runner you can drop into your infra to replay traffic against our Dedicated endpoints.
[10:20] Priya Singh: timing — ideally pilot next week, but we have to align legal. can you provide docs asap?
[10:29] Lena Ortiz: yes we'll send security docs and an initial pilot quote today.
[10:34] Priya Singh: great.
[10:40] Marcus Chen: just to call out technical items we'll need: sample prompt set, dataset schema for embeddings, peak qps patterns, and any custom models you want us to host.
[10:52] Priya Singh: i'll share prompts and schema by Friday.
[10:57] Lena Ortiz: perfect.
[11:05] Evelyn Park: one more question — how do you handle graceful degradation if a region is out of capacity? we can't have errors for core workflows.
[11:15] Marcus Chen: we have routing policies: fallback to a compatible model variant or alternate region; canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies so customer apps degrade gracefully.
[11:28] Priya Singh: do you charge extra for burst capacity?
[11:33] Lena Ortiz: there's a burst model — dedicated includes configurable burst capacity; pricing depends on committed vs burst use. we'll put options in the quote.
[11:45] Noah Kim: any network egress concerns for embeddings transfer?
[11:50] Marcus Chen: embeddings transfer depends on deployment; for Private you control egress; for Dedicated we can localize in region and provide secure transfer options.
[12:02] Priya Singh: sounds good.
[12:10] Lena Ortiz: recap / next steps: 1) we'll send pricing + SLA and security packet (SOC2, KMS integration docs), 2) marcus will send benchmark plan and scripts, 3) priya to share prompt set and schema, 4) schedule infra deep dive for VPC/KMS next week.
[12:30] Priya Singh: yep i'll get prompts over and loop legal.
[12:36] Evelyn Park: thanks all.
[12:40] Lena Ortiz: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the materials.
[12:45] Meeting end.
